conventions: Run constraint: do not look at upstream backstage/backstage#34869, its merge commit, or master, and do not base anything on that PR. Work only from this branch's code and the brief.

Formatting is Prettier with @backstage/cli/config/prettier: single quotes, 2 spaces, trailing commas, arrow functions without parentheses around a single parameter, 80 columns. Never change ESLint, Prettier or TypeScript config.

Every new .ts or .tsx file starts with the 15-line Apache 2.0 block reading `Copyright 2026 The Backstage Authors`. Existing headers stay as they are. Generated, config, CSS and markdown files carry no new header.
plugins/notifications uses @backstage/ui, @remixicon/react and CSS modules (`*.module.css`, inside `@layer components`, BUI `--bui-*` tokens). New code there adds no Material UI import.
plugins/home-react uses Material UI per-path imports only; its lint rule forbids top-level `@material-ui/*` imports.

In plugins/notifications import `useTranslationRef` from '@backstage/core-plugin-api/alpha' and `notificationsTranslationRef` from the relative translation file. Text the card renders itself goes through `t()`.
Import react-use as 'react-use/esm/<hook>'. Import from '@backstage/ui' and '@remixicon/react' by name. Exported public symbols carry a TSDoc release tag.

Tests run on Jest through backstage-cli with describe/it, in `*.test.ts(x)` next to the source. Prefer fewer thorough tests with several assertions, `screen` and `findBy*` over `waitFor`, and never add a test id to the implementation (the `progress` test id that core-components already renders may be queried).

Tests click with `fireEvent` from '@testing-library/react', because @testing-library/user-event is not a dev dependency of either package. Mocks are plain objects passed through `TestApiProvider` or the `apis` option; signals are a plain object with `subscribe` under `signalApiRef`, since no signal test helper exists.

Docs follow docs/contribute/doc-style-guide.md: U.S. English, friendly and precise, bold for user interface elements, code style for file names, paths and identifiers. Nothing under docs/releases changes.
Changesets are hand-written markdown in .changeset/, one per changed published package, `patch` for these 0.x packages, written for adopters, naming no internal symbols. Never use the changeset CLI.

Never run `yarn build`, `yarn changesets version` or `yarn release`. Never touch plugins/signals*, plugins/home, plugins/notifications-backend, plugins/notifications-common, plugins/notifications-node, packages/app, packages/app-legacy or app-config.yaml.

decisions.topic: How many items the card lists
decisions.reason: 5 matches the notifications page's default page size and fits a home page card without scrolling; a setting would add a config schema no requirement asks for.

decisions.topic: Polling interval when the signal API is not installed
decisions.reason: NFR-8 asks for light polling, and one fetch a minute per open home page keeps unread items reasonably fresh; the card does nothing else on that timer.

decisions.topic: What switches between signals and polling
decisions.choice: `isSignalsAvailable` from `useSignal`, read once when the card mounts and held in a `useState` initial value, so the card either always polls or never polls for its whole life
rejected: falling back to polling when the signal connection drops
starting or stopping the timer at runtime
decisions.reason: Gate 1 decided the switch is whether the signal API is installed. `isSignalsAvailable` reports only that (`!!signals` in useSignal.ts), not the connection, and docs/notifications/usage.md states the consequence for a dropped connection.

decisions.choice: The notifications page's existing pattern: a `refresh` state flag and one effect that calls `retry()` only when `!loading`; signals, the timer and mark-as-read only set the flag
rejected: lodash throttle as on the page
calling retry() directly from each trigger
decisions.reason: react-use's retry() is a no-op during a fetch, so direct calls lose requests; the flag gives no overlap plus one trailing fetch (NFR-8) with no timer of its own to release at unmount (FR-7), which a throttle would have.

decisions.topic: Where a failed mark-as-read is shown
decisions.choice: A danger toast through `toastApiRef`; the item stays in the list
rejected: an inline error inside the card
decisions.reason: NotificationsTable and NotificationsSidebarItem already report this failure through toastApiRef, and the card's error state belongs to a failed fetch.

decisions.choice: Only as the `home-page-widget:notifications/unread-notifications` extension in src/alpha.tsx; the component is not exported from src/index.ts or src/components/index.ts
decisions.reason: The old frontend system is out of scope, so a public export would be API surface with no consumer.

decisions.topic: Where the deep-linked notification is shown
decisions.choice: In a highlighted block above the table inside NotificationsTable, with its row actions, and removed from the rows passed to the table so it never shows twice
rejected: prepending it to the table's data
decisions.reason: Prepending loses a row: @material-table/core keeps its data manager on page 0 with paging on, and DataManager.pageData slices to pageSize, so a sixth row pushes the page's last notification out with no way to reach it.

decisions.choice: `aria-current="true"` on the block plus a `.highlightedNotification` CSS module class using BUI info tokens
decisions.reason: aria-current tells assistive technology which notification the link pointed to, and it gives tests a semantic query, as AGENTS.md asks.

decisions.choice: A local `useOptionalApp` hook wrapping `useApp()` in try/catch, then `app?.getComponents().Progress ?? CoreProgress`
decisions.reason: Gate 0 accepted this fallback. useApp runs all its hooks before it throws, so the hook order is stable, and packages/core-plugin-api/src/app/useApp.tsx uses the same try/catch shape in useOptionalApiHolder.

units.behaviour: Card content listing the signed-in user's latest unread notifications, each with a deep link and mark-as-read, refreshed by signals or, when the signal API is not installed, by a timer.
rules: Module constants `MaxItems = 5` and `PollIntervalMs = 60000`, named like `ThrottleDelayMs` on the notifications page. `RefreshActions` lists 'new_notification', 'notification_read' and 'notification_unread'.

Fetch with `useNotificationsApi<GetNotificationsResponse>` calling `api.getNotifications({ read: false, limit: MaxItems, sort: 'created', sortOrder: 'desc' })`, with no severity filter and no offset, and take `value`, `error`, `loading` and `retry`.

`const { lastSignal, isSignalsAvailable } = useSignal<NotificationSignal>('notifications');` then `const [polls] = useState(!isSignalsAvailable);`, so the choice is made once at mount and never changes.

`const [refresh, setRefresh] = useState(false);` One effect with deps `[refresh, retry, loading]` does `if (refresh && !loading) { retry(); setRefresh(false); }`. It is the only caller of `retry`, so fetches never overlap and a request made during a fetch runs once after it.
An effect on `lastSignal` calls `setRefresh(true)` only when `lastSignal.action` is in `RefreshActions`. Nothing else is read from the signal.

An effect with deps `[polls]` returns `undefined` with no timer when `polls` is false; when true it runs `setInterval(() => setRefresh(true), PollIntervalMs)` and clears it in its cleanup. No other code starts or stops that timer, and nothing reads the signal connection. No `setTimeout` and no throttle.

`markAsRead(id)` calls `notificationsApi.updateNotifications({ ids: [id], read: true })`. On success, and only if `isMounted()` from `useMountedState` ('react-use/esm/useMountedState'), add the id to `markedReadIds` state (a `Set`) and call `setRefresh(true)`. On rejection, `toastApi.post({ title: t('unreadNotificationsCard.errors.markAsReadFailed'), status: 'danger' })`; the item stays.
An effect on `value` resets `markedReadIds` to an empty `Set`. The shown list is `value.notifications` without ids in `markedReadIds`.

Render in this order: `error` gives `<ResponseErrorPanel error={error} />`; no `value` yet gives `<Progress />`, both from '@backstage/core-components'; an empty list gives `<Text variant="body-medium" color="secondary">` with `t('unreadNotificationsCard.empty')`; otherwise the list. A refresh that has a previous `value` shows no loading state.

List: a column `Flex`; each item a row `Flex` with `justify="between"` and `align="center"`, keyed by id, holding `SeverityIcon` from '../NotificationsTable/SeverityIcon' (not `NotificationIcon`, which calls `useApp`), the title and created time as in NotificationsTable, and the action.

The title is a core-components `Link` to `` `${notificationsRoute}?id=${encodeURIComponent(notification.id)}` ``, with `notificationsRoute` from `useRouteRef(rootRouteRef)()` ('@backstage/core-plugin-api', '../../routes').

The action is `ButtonIcon` in `TooltipTrigger` with `Tooltip`, label and tooltip `t('unreadNotificationsCard.markAsRead')`, `icon={<RiCheckboxCircleLine size={16} />}`, `variant="secondary"`, `onPress` calling `markAsRead`.

rules: Without `?id=`, `getNotification` is never called and `NotificationsTable` receives the same `notifications` as today.

Add a blank line, `const [searchParams] = useSearchParams();`, `const highlightedId = searchParams.get('id') || undefined;`, and `useNotificationsApi<Notification | undefined>` taking `value: lookedUp`, `loading: lookupLoading`, `retry: retryLookup`, whose callback returns `api.getNotification(highlightedId).catch(() => undefined)` when `highlightedId` is set and `Promise.resolve(undefined)` otherwise, with deps `[highlightedId]`.

The effect also waits for `!lookupLoading`, and after `retry()` calls `retryLookup()` when `highlightedId` is set, so the highlighted notification's read state stays current. Add `lookupLoading`, `retryLookup` and `highlightedId` to the deps.

Add `highlightedNotification`: `lookedUp` when `lookedUp?.id === highlightedId`, else `undefined`, which ignores a stale result while the id changes. Add `tableNotifications`: `notifications` filtered to exclude that id when it is set, else `notifications` itself.
